texts.preamble: P.Pavithran vs State-Rep.By Public Prosecutor on 12 January, 2016 Author: B.Sudheendra Kumar Bench: B.Sudheendra Kumar In The High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam Present: The Honourable Mr. Justice B.Sudheendra Kumar Tuesday, The 12Th Day Of January 2016/22Nd Pousha, 1937 Crl.Rev.Pet.No. 1642 of 2006 ( ) --------------------------------- Crl.A 64/2000 of Addl.Sessions Court (Adhoc)-Iii, Thalassery Cc 382/1999 of Addl.C.J.M.,Thalassery Revision Petitioner(S)/Appellants/Accused: ----------------------------------------------------------------------- 1. P.Pavithran,Salesman, Ksheera Vyavasaya Sahakarana Sangam Ltd. Thalassery. 2. S.T.Jaison,Secretary, Ksheera Vyavasaya Sahakarana Sangam Ltd. Thalassery . 3. P.P.Gopalan,President, Ksheera Vyavasaya Sahakarana Sangam Ltd. Thalassery. 4. The Thalassery Ksheera Vyavasaya Sahakarana Sangam Ltd., Rep.By Its Secretary. By Advs.Sri.M.Sasindran Sri.M.B.Prajith Respondent(S)/Respondents/Complainant:
texts.facts: on the files of the Court of the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Thalassery filed this Revision Petition challenging the concurrent finding of conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Sections 2(i)(m) and 7(i)(a) read with Section 16(1) (a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. 2. Heard. 3. The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:- On 26.8.2005 at about 10 a.m., PW1, the Food Inspector, purchased 900 gram of milk ice from the shop of the first accused. Second accused was the licensee of the said shop. Fourth accused was the manufacture and third accused was the President of fourth accused. After sampling as per rules, one of the samples was sent for analysis to the Public Analyst. The Public Analyst filed Ext. P11 report stating that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for milk ice under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1956 and therefore, the same was adulterated. Thereafter, on the request of the accused, second sample was sent to the Central Food Laboratory for analysis. Ext.P14 report of the Central Food Laboratory would show that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for milk ice and therefore, it was adulterated. 4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW3 were examined and Exts. P1 to P23 series were marked for the prosecution. DW1 was examined and Ext.D1 was marked for the revision petitioners. By Public Prosecutor on 12 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193766918/ 2 mandate of Section 23 (1-A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act, Ext. P14 cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased by the Food Inspector was adulterated.
texts.arguments: 5. The learned counsel for the revision petitioners has submitted that since no laboratory for the analysis of the food item was defined and no validated method of analysis was prescribed as per the P.Pavithran vs State-Rep. The learned counsel for the revision petitioners relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176] to buttress his argument. 6. In this case, admittedly, the laboratory for the analysis of food item was not defined and no validated method of analysis of the food item was prescribed as mandated under Section 23 (1-A) (ee) and (hh) of the P.F.A. Act. Therefore, Ext. P14 certificate of analysis cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased in this case was adulterated in view of the decision of the Apex court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra). It was held by the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) that since the Laboratories were not notified and the tests conducted by such laboratories were not admissible in evidence, no prosecution could be based on such report and the accused was entitled to get acquittal. In the decision of this Court in Gopalakrishnan v. Food Inspector [2013 (3) KLT 455], the court relied on the decision of the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) and found that the Public Analyst's report was not admissible in evidence and accordingly, the Court acquitted the accused.
